context:
Start with w1 (pure config cleanup, zero risk, unblocks nothing but is
trivial to land first). w2 and w3 are independent and can proceed in
parallel - both are "add or re-mark fast tests for an under-tested
module" with the same shape. Measure actual runtime with
`pytest --durations=0` before deciding fast vs. keep-medium for w2's
existing test file. w4 depends on w2+w3 landing since it removes the
omit entry only once real fast-lane coverage exists to replace it.
description:
Test-strategy review of coverage configuration found real coverage
blind spots, but the originally-cited facts needed correction after
reading the current tree - two of the three "omitted" TPC-DI ETL files
no longer exist:

`.coveragerc_core:16-18` currently reads:

    benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/transformations.py
    benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/batch.py
    benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py

- `transformations.py` was deleted in commit `0fbbd431` ("chore: shrink
  dead TPC-DI transformations (#640)").
- `batch.py` was deleted in commit `5b15277b` ("chore: shrink dead TPC-DI
  ETL batch scaffold (#637)").
- Both omit entries are now stale/dead config referring to files that
  don't exist - harmless (coverage's `omit` glob just matches nothing)
  but should be cleaned up so the file doesn't misrepresent what's
  actually being excluded from coverage.
- `scd_processor.py` DOES still exist (951 lines,
  `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py`) and IS still omitted from
  coverage entirely. It has a dedicated unit test file
  (`tests/unit/core/tpcdi/test_etl_scd_processor.py`, marked
  `pytest.mark.unit, pytest.mark.medium` - not `fast`) plus exercise via
  `tests/integration/test_tpcdi_phase3_benchmark.py` (`integration,
  medium`) and `tests/integration/test_tpcdi_full_benchmark.py`
  (`integration, slow`). None of these run in the fast lane
  (`-m "fast and not (slow or ...)"`, `.github/workflows/pr.yml:450`,
  `--cov-fail-under=70`), so even without the coverage omit,
  `scd_processor.py` contributes zero coverage to the number CI actually
  gates on - the omit just also hides it from the full/nightly coverage
  report.

Separately, `benchbox/core/throughput/` (`runner.py` 163 lines,
`result.py` 72 lines - imported by
`benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py` and
`benchbox/core/tpcds/throughput_test.py`) is NOT in the `.coveragerc_core`
omit list, so it's nominally measured - but its only real exerciser,
`tests/integration/test_tpch_throughput_test.py`, is marked
`pytest.mark.integration, pytest.mark.slow`. There is no
`fast`-marked test that imports or exercises `core/throughput` at all,
so its real fast-lane coverage is effectively zero even though the
90-line-ish module isn't formally excluded.

Net effect: the 70% `--cov-fail-under` floor
(`.github/workflows/pr.yml:450`) is measured only on the fast lane, and
two real modules (`scd_processor.py`, `core/throughput/`) have no
fast-lane characterization tests protecting them from regressions
between releases, even though one of them isn't even coverage-omitted.

anti_patterns.dont: attempt to characterize real multi-threaded timing/concurrency behavior of core/throughput/runner.py in fast tests
anti_patterns.instead: keep the fast tests to pure/deterministic logic and leave timing behavior to the existing slow integration test.
anti_patterns.why: that inherently requires wall-clock-sensitive execution unsuitable for a fast deterministic lane

anti_patterns.dont: mark test_etl_scd_processor.py or new throughput tests 'fast' without measuring actual runtime first
anti_patterns.why: mis-marking a slow test as fast defeats the purpose of the lane split and can make the required PR gate flaky/slow

anti_patterns.dont: re-add omit entries for transformations.py / batch.py 'just in case'
anti_patterns.instead: if they come back, that's a new decision for a new commit, not a reason to keep stale references now.
anti_patterns.why: they were deliberately deleted as dead code by #637/#640

preserves.behavior: Existing medium/slow/integration TPC-DI and throughput tests (test_etl_scd_processor.py if left as medium, test_tpcdi_phase3_benchmark.py, test_tpcdi_full_benchmark.py, test_tpch_throughput_test.py) continue to pass unchanged.
No behavior change to benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py or benchbox/core/throughput/ - this is a test-and-config-only TODO.
The 70% --cov-fail-under floor in .github/workflows/pr.yml:450 continues to pass after adding new fast tests (new tests should raise coverage, not just add runtime).

verifications.expected: Exit 0 (grep found no match; bare grep exits 1 on no-match, so it must be inverted for this to be a pass/fail gate)

verifications.description: New/re-marked fast tests for scd_processor.py pass and are collected in the fast lane
verifications.expected: Tests collected and pass under the fast marker

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/throughput/ -m fast -v
verifications.description: New fast tests for core/throughput pass and are collected in the fast lane
verifications.expected: Tests collected and pass under the fast marker

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -m "fast and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)" --cov=benchbox --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=70
verifications.description: Fast-lane coverage floor still passes with the coveragerc omissions removed

Delete the `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/transformations.py` and
`benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/batch.py` lines from `.coveragerc_core`'s
`omit` list (lines 16-17) - both files were removed by #640 and #637

work_units.summary: Remove the two stale .coveragerc_core omit entries for deleted files

work_units.notes:
`tests/unit/core/tpcdi/test_etl_scd_processor.py` already exists and
is well-scoped (104 lines) but marked `medium`, not `fast`. Two
options, pick based on actual runtime once measured:
  1. If the existing medium tests are individually fast (likely,
     given SCD logic is pure in-memory transformation, not I/O), just
     re-mark the file's `pytestmark` to `fast` after confirming
     runtime with `--durations=0`.
  2. If the existing tests are genuinely slower (e.g. they spin up a
     DataFrame/DB fixture), add a small new `fast`-marked test module
     covering the core SCD Type-2 branching logic
     (insert-new-version / expire-old-version / no-op-unchanged)
     against minimal in-memory fixtures, leaving the existing
     `medium` file for broader integration-shaped cases.
Whichever path, the fast lane must end up covering scd_processor.py.
work_units.summary: Add fast-marked characterization tests for benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py

work_units.notes:
`benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py` (163 lines) and `result.py`
(72 lines) currently have no test coverage outside the slow-marked
`tests/integration/test_tpch_throughput_test.py`. Add a small
`fast`-marked unit test module (e.g.
`tests/unit/core/throughput/test_runner.py`) covering the runner's
pure logic paths with a mocked/fake benchmark object (mirroring the
pattern already used in test_tpch_throughput_test.py's
`benchmark.get_query.return_value = "SELECT 1"` style mocking, but
without the `slow` marker) - concurrency/throughput timing behavior,
result aggregation in `result.py`, and error/edge-case handling
(zero queries, single-thread fallback, etc.). Do not attempt to
characterize actual multi-threaded timing behavior in the fast lane -
that's what the existing slow integration test is for; focus fast
tests on deterministic logic (aggregation math, config validation,
result-shape correctness).
work_units.summary: Add fast-marked characterization tests for benchbox/core/throughput/

work_units.notes:
Once w2/w3 land fast-lane coverage for scd_processor.py (and
core/throughput if it turns out to need adding to the omit list
pending w3 - it currently is NOT omitted, so no removal needed
there), remove the now-covered `scd_processor.py` line from

comment above it in `.coveragerc_core` explaining WHY it's

exercised via golden-output tests, not line coverage" or
"# experimental, not on any release-gate path") so future readers
don't have to archaeology their way to an answer the way this TODO
had to.
